subject: MAP: commitment-readiness & pricing pulse
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@voltware.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: commitment-readiness & pricing pulse

Hi Sophie + Voltware team,

Quick weekly checkpoint following our MAP meeting last week. Goal here is to make sure pricing/credits and commit sizing are aligned so we hit the target close window (targeting EoNQ close).

Key items for this update:
- Outstanding discount ask: Voltware requested 25% off list for a 12-month committed consumption of $600k (quarterly cadence).
- Internal credit ask: Voltware requested $30k onboarding credit to offset integration costs.
- Open approvals: any discount >20% requires Sales Ops sign-off and Finance pre-approval of credit.
- Evaluation extension: Sophie asked for a 2-week evaluation extension on the production sandbox to finalize acceptance tests.

Attachments: Voltware-MAP-v1.3.pdf (latest MAP with milestones), pricing-summary-vw.xlsx (proposal line items).

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Ben — escalate 25% discount request to Sales Ops and provide play-by-play on required approvals (target: 48 hours).
2) Neha — confirm Finance comfort with $30k onboarding credit and whether credit should be amortized vs. one-time payment (target: EOD Wed).
3) Marissa — capture acceptance criteria for the evaluation extension and confirm support coverage during the extra 2 weeks (target: tomorrow).
4) Sophie / Voltware — confirm if the commit sizing can be firmed to $600k or if they prefer a stepped commit (e.g., $450k Q1 then $150k ramp).

If we can close approvals by next Thursday we can align DocuSign and start provisioning dedicated capacity the following week.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@voltware.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@voltware.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: commitment-readiness & pricing pulse

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear checklist. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 25% ask is our preferred path if Sales can confirm predictable unit economics. If Sales Ops needs a business case we can share a short TCO slide (I can pull the numbers).
- Onboarding credit: $30k one-time is what Procurement prefers (helps our implementation team). If Finance asks to amortize, we'll need a clear schedule.
- Evaluation extension: yes, we need the +2 weeks on the prod sandbox. We need a named Redwood contact for availability windows (Mon-Fri PST) and an SLO for incident response during the evaluation.

We can commit to either firm $600k or a stepped commit — our execs prefer the stepped approach with a firm $450k Q1 and an optional $150k ramp after acceptance. That gives them runway for FY planning.

I'll attach the TCO once I have it. For now, can your team confirm who will be the Sales Ops reviewer and whether Finance needs additional paperwork to approve onboarding credits?

— Sophie
Sophie Lemaire
VP, Partnerships | Voltware
sophie.lemaire@voltware.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: commitment-readiness & pricing pulse

Looping through Finance alignment. Quick internal summary: 

- Onboarding credit ($30k): Finance is provisionally OK with a one-time credit provided it is coded to onboarding (CAPEX vs. OPEX conversation to follow). We need the contract clause that specifies credit timing and an invoice schedule.
- Discount band: Finance will not sign off on a flat 25% without Sales Ops assessing pipeline uplift and risk —— we can support a 15% baseline discount without escalation. Anything >20% requires Sales Ops review and AP approval.
- Commit structure: Finance prefers firm commitments where possible; a stepped commit (450k firm + optional 150k) is acceptable if Voltware signs a mutual ramp clause in the MAP (we'll ask Legal to draft).

Action items assigned: 
- Ben: escalate 25% ask to Sales Ops (include the attached pricing-summary-vw.xlsx and the MAP PDF). Call out precedent deals and recommended margin preservation levers (e.g., rate cards, limited free tokens during ramp).
- Marissa: draft the acceptance criteria and operational SLOs for the +2 week evaluation (include named contacts/support windows).
- Rafael: coordinate with Sophie for final TCO doc and confirm if Voltware wants the stepped commit language.

I will block time with Finance for an expedited review once Sales Ops confirms whether they will approve >20%.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance Partnerships | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: commitment-readiness & pricing pulse

Quick update — I escalated the 25% discount request to Sales Ops (ticket INC-8721) and included the MAP + pricing XLS. Sales Ops (Karthik) asked for a short rundown of comparable deals; I pulled 3 recent comps and recommended the following: approve 22% if Voltware takes the stepped commit and we amortize the onboarding credit over 4 quarters; escalate >22% to SVP approval.

Next steps for the thread:
- I will post the Sales Ops outcome in HubSpot and link DocuSign once we have final language (aim: Wed EOD).
- Marissa, coordinate with Support to lock an on-call for the evaluation extension and add the named contact in the MAP.

Ben
